title: CNC router: stepper motors, ball screws, linear rails and spindle
summary: A CNC router gives you 3–4 NEMA 23 stepper motors, ball screws or lead screws, hardened linear rails and bearing blocks, an aluminium extrusion frame, a spindle or trim router and a 36–48 V power supply. Allow about 90 minutes for a hobby machine, much longer for a big one. The main dangers are a gantry or Z axis that drops when its screw is freed, and charge left in spindle drives.

steps.text: Unplug the machine from the wall, then unplug the trim router or the spindle cable at the control box. Take the cutter out first: loosen the collet nut and slide the bit out, holding it in a rag. Wear gloves for all the work: edges, chips and swarf are sharp.
steps.warn: The emergency stop button is not an isolator. Pull the mains plug, and pull the bit before you touch anything else.

steps.text: Open the control box. Photograph it and label every connector with tape (each motor, limit switch, spindle, e-stop). With the meter, prove the mains terminals are dead. Wait 5 minutes, then measure DC volts across the power terminals of any spindle drive (VFD) or servo drive. Over about 30 V, discharge with a resistor tool (see safety_discharge_capacitor) and measure again.
steps.warn: Spindle and servo drives can hold 300–600 V DC after unplugging. Don't touch their terminals until the meter reads near zero.

steps.text: Remove the spindle. Water-cooled: lift the coolant hoses off over a bucket and empty the loop, then take out the pump with its cord. Unplug the spindle cable (a threaded 3- or 4-pin plug). Hold the spindle with one hand while you undo its clamp bolts: 3-phase spindles weigh 4–8 kg, trim routers 2–3 kg.
steps.warn: Don't let coolant run into the control box. Mop up spills before they reach a wire.

steps.text: Take off the spoilboard and any clamps. Bring the Z carriage (the one the spindle hung on) down to the bottom of its travel by turning its screw by hand at the motor end, or support it on a wooden block, before you free its motor or screw.
steps.warn: Ball screws are not self-locking. Once the motor is off, a carriage or gantry can slide down on its own and crush fingers.

steps.text: Remove the stepper motors one at a time. Unplug the lead, undo the 4 bolts through the flange and slide the motor out of its mount. Undo the grub screw on the coupler or pulley and keep it with the motor. Read the label (volts, amps, holding torque) and write it on a strip of tape on the motor.

Free each screw. Undo the nut block from the carriage, then the end-support bearing blocks, and slide the screw out. Keep a ball nut on its screw: tape it in place and never run it off the end of the thread. Wrap the screw in cardboard and store it flat or hanging.
steps.warn: A ball nut slid off its screw spills its balls everywhere and is very hard to refill. Keep it taped on.

steps.text: Take the linear rails and carriages. Undo the rail bolts through the access holes with a hex key. Keep each carriage on its rail. Tape over the rail ends so a block can't slide off and drop its balls. Wrap the rails in cloth or cardboard.

Lift out the gantry. Support it from underneath, undo its mounting bolts and take it off with a helper. Then unscrew the extrusion frame at its corner brackets with a hex key. Slide T-nuts, brackets and plates onto a wire or string so they stay together.
steps.warn: A gantry weighs 20–60 kg and is top-heavy. Two people, and stand where it can't tip onto you.

steps.text: Take the control box parts: the 36–48 V power supply, stepper driver modules, the controller board, the VFD, relays, fans, the e-stop button, the homing or limit switches (inductive, Hall or micro-switch, with their leads) and the wiring. Snip cables long and keep the plugs on.
Bag the small parts: couplers, pulleys, belts, bearings, screws. Before you sweep up, put on a mask: MDF, phenolic and aluminium dust are fine and harmful to breathe.

notes:
## What's worth keeping and why

- **Stepper motors.** NEMA 23 motors have a 57 mm square flange, 1–3 Nm holding torque and 2–4 A per phase. They are the best precision drive you can salvage. Run them from stepper driver modules for positioning, or use them as slow high-torque drives for a winch, feeder or small mill. To sort the wires of an unmarked motor, measure resistance: the two wires of one coil read a few ohms, wires of different coils read open.
- **Ball screws, lead screws and linear rails.** Ground screws and hardened rails give accurate straight-line motion for a small lathe or mill carriage, a drill press feed, a press, or a sliding gate. Don't bend them, and keep them oiled.
- **Bearings and couplers.** Pillow blocks, screw-end bearings, couplers and pulleys.
- **Aluminium extrusion.** T-slot profile with brackets and T-nuts: frames, benches, racks and solar mounts, joined with a hex key and no welding.
- **Trim router.** A universal motor of about 1 kW at 10,000–30,000 rpm. Use it as a normal hand router, or on a table. It can run from an inverter.
- **3-phase spindle and VFD.** A 1.5–2.2 kW spindle is a high-speed induction motor (often 24,000 rpm at 400 Hz). It must run from its VFD, which makes 3-phase from single-phase mains. Keep the pair together. The VFD can also run other 3-phase motors of similar power, such as pumps and bench machines.
- **Power supply.** A 36–48 V DC supply of 8–15 A, made to run the steppers.
- **Sensors and e-stop.** Inductive proximity sensors (5–30 V) and Hall switches make limit switches and counters. A heavy mushroom e-stop button is good for any machine you build.
- **Fans and coolant pump.** Control box fans and a small mains pump.

## Variations

- Hobby machines (Shapeoko, Onefinity and 3018 types) use steppers, belts or lead screws and a trim router, and weigh 30–60 kg.
- Industrial routers are 2–3 m long and can weigh half a tonne or more. They use rack-and-pinion drives, servo motors and a large VFD, and may have a vacuum pump and a compressed-air tool changer. Take the loose parts and leave the frame unless you have lifting gear (see safety_lifting).
- Servo motors need a matching drive, so keep each motor with its encoder cable and its drive.

## What to leave

- The MDF spoilboard and plastic dust shoe.
- A bent or damaged screw or rail.
